'''Ionica Smeets''' (born 8 October 1979) is a [[Dutch people|Dutch]] mathematician, [[science journalist]], columnist, television presenter and professor in [[science communication]] at [[Leiden University]].

==Biography==
Ionica Smeets was born in [[Delft]], where she completed her [[propedeuse]] in [[computer science]] at the [[Delft University of Technology]]. She switched studies and graduated in [[applied mathematics]].

Smeets was working on her thesis in mathematics, on a subject within [[number theory]], at Leiden University when she started the blog ''Wiskundemeisjes'' ('''Math girls''<nowiki/>'), on 14 March 2006, together with Jeanine Daems. The website has been awarded in 2007 with two ''Dutch Bloggies''.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121018221041/http://www.nijghenvanditmar.nl/web/Auteur/Ionica-Smeets.htm Ionica Smeets] Nijgh & Van Ditmar</ref> Since 2010, the two 'math girls' ran a [[Column (periodical)|column]] in ''[[De Volkskrant]]'' for several years. Currently, Smeets writes a weekly piece titled "''Ionica zag een getal''" ("''Ionica saw a number''") in the periodical ''Sir Edmund'' (a magazine from ''[[De Volkskrant]]'').

She completed her PhD at Leiden in 2010; her dissertation, ''On Continued Fraction Algorithms'', was supervised by [[Robert Tijdeman]] and Cornelis Kraaikamp.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=145518}}</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130903135427/http://www.math.leidenuniv.nl/scripties/SmeetsThesis.pdf Ionica Smeets: On continued fraction algorithms, diss. Univ Leiden 2010]</ref>
After this, Smeets became a science journalist. She performs research, together with [[Bas Haring]], on successful methods to explain science to the general audience. In this function, she appeared on Dutch television, such as in ''[[De Wereld Draait Door]]''. On 19 October 2011, the book ''Ik was altijd heel slecht in wiskunde'' (''I have always been bad at mathematics'') appeared, which she wrote together with Jeanine Daems. Begin 2012, Smeets co-presented eight editions of the [[KRO]]-program ''De Rekenkamer'', replacing [[Sofie van den Enk]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120113121552/http://derekenkamer.kro.nl/ionica_smeets Ionica Smeets] De Rekenkamer</ref> In 2013, Smeets presented the mathematics program ''Eureka'', together with Van den Enk.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131017091212/http://pers.kro.nl/programmas/eureka Eureka]</ref> On 17 August 2014 she was guest in the Dutch television program ''Zomergasten''. Furthermore, she participated in the [[NCRV]]'s [[Quiz|television quiz]] ''[[De slimste mens|De Slimste Mens]]'' in August 2014, almost reaching the final round.<ref>[http://www.televizier.nl/nieuws/actualiteiten/waarom-haalde-ionica-smeets-niet-de-finaleweek.3893408.lynkx Televizier.nl]"</ref>

In July 2015, Smeets was appointed professor in Science Communication at the University of Leiden.<ref>[http://www.volkskrant.nl/wetenschap/van-wiskundemeisje-tot-hoogleraar-communicatie~a4094154 De Volkskrant (4 juli 2015): Van 'wiskundemeisje' tot hoogleraar communicatie]</ref> In December 2015, she started presenting the [[VPRO]] television program ''de Nationale Wetenschapsquiz'' (''the National Science Quiz''), which she has presented together with Pieter Hulst up until now.

== Selected publications ==
{{Scholia}}
* Ionica Smeets: ''Zoete kinderen eten geen suiker''. Amsterdam, Uitgeverij Nieuwezijds, 2016. {{ISBN|978-90-5712-467-9}}
* Ionica Smeets: ''Het exacte verhaal''. Amsterdam, Nieuwezijds, 2014. {{ISBN|978-90-571-2393-1}}
* Jeanine Daems & Ionica Smeets: ''Ik was altijd heel slecht in wiskunde. Reken maar op de wiskundemeisjes''. Amsterdam, Nieuwezijds, 2011. {{ISBN|978-90-5712-336-8}}
* Ionica Smeets & Bas Haring: ''Vallende kwartjes. Een slimme selectie van leesbare wetenschap''. Amsterdam, Nijgh & Van Ditmar 2010. 5th print 2012: {{ISBN|978-90-388-9485-0}}
* Ionica Smeets: ''On continued fraction algorithms''. Enschede, Ipskamp Drukkers, 2010. (Proefschrift Universiteit Leiden) No ISBN. [[hdl:1887/15693|Digital version]]
